_meta.description: Literature anchors for the constants of the energy module. Same contract as src/rules/catalog.json: every entry carries source + evidenceLevel, and the numeric values are the ones the code actually uses (config defaults). evidenceLevel scale: meta-analysis > rct > cohort > expert-consensus > assumption. Entries marked 'assumption' are transparent extensions, not literature — see the kickoff doc.

entries.name: Mifflin-St Jeor
entries.source: Mifflin MD, St Jeor ST et al. (1990), Am J Clin Nutr 51(2):241-247 — a new predictive equation for resting energy expenditure in healthy individuals. The best-validated general-population BMR equation.

entries.name: Owen
entries.source: Owen OE et al. (1986), Am J Clin Nutr 44(1):1-19 (women) and (1987) 46(6):875-885 (men) — a reappraisal of the caloric requirements of healthy adults. Weight-only, therefore insensitive to height and age.

entries.name: Katch-McArdle
entries.source: Katch FI, McArdle WD — Exercise Physiology: Energy, Nutrition and Human Performance. Fat-free-mass based, so it needs a body-composition estimate; it does not inherit the sex term the weight-based equations carry.

entries.name: Harris-Benedict (1918 original)
entries.source: Harris JA, Benedict FG (1918), PNAS 4(12):370-373 — a biometric study of basal metabolism in man. Overestimates on modern cohorts by roughly 5 %; kept selectable for comparison, never a default.

entries.name: Cunningham
entries.source: Cunningham JJ (1980), Am J Clin Nutr 33(11):2372-2374 — a reanalysis of the factors influencing basal metabolic rate in normal adults. Calibrated on lean, trained subjects and overestimates outside that group.

entries.name: Atwater factors
entries.source: Atwater general factor system, as codified in FAO Food and Nutrition Paper 77 (2003). The fibre factor is a labelling convention, not a measurement: EU Regulation 1169/2011 Annex XIV uses 2 kcal/g, the US (21 CFR 101.9) treats fibre as 4 kcal/g carbohydrate. At 35 g/day that is a 70 kcal difference.

entries.name: Thermic effect of food, per macronutrient
entries.source: Westerterp KR (2004), Nutr Metab 1:5 — diet induced thermogenesis. Reported ranges: protein 20-30 %, carbohydrate 5-10 %, fat 0-3 %; mixed-diet total ~10 % of intake, which is the fallback when macros are missing.
entries.gap: No coefficient for alcohol is given in the kickoff, so alcohol energy is treated as 0 % TEF rather than guessed. The literature suggests it is not negligible (~15-20 %), which makes this a conservative underestimate of TEF.

entries.name: Energy density of weight change
entries.source: Wishnofsky M (1958), Am J Clin Nutr 6(5):542-546 — the classic 3500 kcal/lb figure for adipose tissue. Known to be a simplification: the fat/fat-free split of the tissue lost varies with body composition (Forbes 1987, Hall 2008). ADR 0006 keeps it a fixed, configurable constant rather than putting a second unvalidated model inside the measured result.

entries.name: Body-fat-aware weekly rate ceiling
entries.source: Graded from the observation that leaner individuals lose proportionally more fat-free mass at a given deficit (Forbes 1987; Hall 2007). The specific band edges and rates are a practitioner convention, not a measured threshold.

entries.name: Maximum deficit per kg fat mass
entries.source: Alpert SS (2005), Nutrition 21(11-12):1129-1132 — a limit on the rate at which adipose tissue can mobilise energy, above which the shortfall is met from lean tissue. The 30 kcal/kg figure is the commonly cited practitioner rounding of that limit, not Alpert's own coefficient.

entries.name: Low energy availability threshold
entries.source: Loucks AB, Thuma JR (2003), J Clin Endocrinol Metab 88(1):297-311 — LH pulsatility is disrupted below roughly 30 kcal/kg FFM. Mountjoy M et al. (2023), Br J Sports Med — IOC consensus on REDs.
entries.gap: Lowering the threshold with rising body fat (eaBodyFatAware) is NOT covered by this literature. The EA cut-offs come from lean athlete cohorts; at 28 % body fat the endogenous reserve is large. Physiologically plausible, deliberately unvalidated — see the kickoff, 'Energieverfügbarkeit'.

entries.name: Full compensation of training energy
entries.source: Torstveit MK et al. (2018), Int J Sport Nutr Exerc Metab — within-day energy deficiency: athletes with suppressed resting metabolic rate spent markedly more time below -400 kcal at an identical 24 h balance, alongside higher cortisol. Murlasits Z et al. (2025), systematic review — matching intake to expenditure in time rather than over the day.

entries.name: Continuous auto-phase rate
entries.source: No literature. The kickoff asks for continuously scaling phases but does not give a curve, so the rate interpolates the max_rate_body_fat_aware bands and takes a fixed share of them — phase and safety ceiling then read one table and cannot drift apart. The share is judgement: 0.70 is the largest value that never touches the ceiling, but at 0.70 the fat-mass deficit cap and the hard intake floor bind for the whole cut and the curve stops steering anything. 0.45 stays clear of both and lands within about 0.05 pp of the hand-written phase ladder in the kickoff's own config.

entries.name: Body-fat-aware EA threshold
entries.source: No literature, and deliberately so — see the gap on energy_availability. The 30 kcal/kg FFM cut-off comes from lean athlete cohorts (Loucks 2003); at 28 % body fat the endogenous reserve is large and a flat threshold produces false positives. The two body-fat anchors reuse the max_rate_body_fat_aware band edges, so only the floor is a new number.
entries.gap: Physiologically plausible, not evidence-based. Load-bearing rather than cosmetic: at 27.9 % body fat the module's own recommended rest-day intake yields EA 28.2 kcal/kg FFM, so against the flat threshold of 30 it would raise EA_LOW every rest day indefinitely.

entries.name: Calibration confidence thresholds
entries.source: No literature. The kickoff requires a low/medium/high confidence level but does not define it; these cut-offs are judgement, kept in config so they are visible and changeable rather than buried as literals.
